item.title: LEGO Animation 3 (Grades 1-3) — Mon Aug 3, 9:00 AM
item.description:
This camp is SOLD OUT. Join the waitlist here. Build sets and characters with LEGOs, then create a short stop-motion movie using iPads. Work in groups to add special effects, dialogue, and music! Instructor: Mike Marquez
Source: Charles M. Schulz Museum

item.title: Let's Make Comics (Grades 4–6) — Mon Aug 3, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Get your pencils ready for a week of cartooning, comics, crafts, and animation! Design characters, develop story ideas, sketch live ice skaters at Snoopy’s Home Ice, and craft your own paper toys. Create individual and collaborative comics that bring your ideas to life! Instructor: Angelica Blancas-Mims

Source: Charles M. Schulz Museum

item.title: Snoopy Safari Mini (Grades TK-K) — Mon Aug 3, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Take a creative adventure through Snoopy’s many personas and learn about the animals he impersonates and their habitats. item.title: Sourdough Basics — Tue Aug 4, 10:30 AM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Dive into the world of sourdough baking in this hands-on class! Learn how to create and feed a sourdough starter, master the basics of bulk fermentation, and shape different types of loaves. Along the way, you’ll gain an understanding of timing, technique, and the simple ingredients that make sourdough bread so special. Perfect for beginners ready to explore artisan breadmaking, this workshop gives you both the knowledge and practice to confidently bake at home. You’ll take home: • A lively sourdough starter to keep your baking journey going. • One pre-bulk fermented loaf, shaped in class, ready to bake the same day. • One freshly mixed boule to ferment overnight and bake the next day.
Source: Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: The Art of Visible Mending: Woven Darning — Tue Aug 4, 4:00 PM — Gather Sebastopol
item.description:
Learn how to repair clothing with woven darning—a functional and beautiful technique especially suited for knitwear. This workshop covers material selection, setting up a darn, and weaving strong, expressive patches. In this workshop you’ll: • Choose yarns and materials for woven darning • Set up and weave a stable darn • Explore design choices for creative, visible repairs • Bring a garment to mend, or use provided samples. Materials included; no experience required.

Guided through a series of richly imagined rooms inside the historic Manor House, guests will move from the legend of the stag to the intrigue of Prohibition and beyond. Along the way, hidden details, sensory moments, and a few unexpected discoveries invite you deeper into the story.

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Aug 6, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem

item.description: “Step out around midnight in early August and you’ll likely see a sky of “falling stars.” This summer delight is part of the Perseids, our best known meteor shower. But what causes it, and why does it occur at the same time each year? Even more intriguing, what prompted its source comet to shift from an expected collision course with Earth? Come learn about the friendly forces in our solar system and how they still give us brilliant fireworks every August, albeit from a safer distance. This Focus Night is intended to prepare you for a Perseids “peak” experience. Unlike planets that can hang around for months, a meteor shower is only visible over a short period of time. You will learn about different kinds of showers, why most are best viewed after midnight, and how to understand what you’re seeing. In celebration of the Summer Solstice, we have a special tasting of all five wines from our Pinot Hill vineyard. Experience the difference in morning and afternoon sunlight when tasting the Pinot Hill East and West. This tasting is only offered once a year, so don’t miss out!
Source: Sebastopol Calendar

item.title: Suzanne Jacquot, Art at La Crema Winery — Tue Aug 11, 10:00 AM — D
item.description:
Suzanne Jacquot Art is currently showing 18 works of art on paper and canvas. Suzanne's art is inspired by her daily walks in nature throughout Sonoma County's trails and parks. She has found each day a new adventure and delights in both the outward chaos and inward inherent structure of nature. The times of day and the seasons bring with it different and exciting color palettes. Location: La Crema Winery, 3575 Slusser Rd, Windsor, CA 95492 Time: Tuesday thru Sunday 10am - 5pm. Dates: Opens July 2026 and continues til July 207.
Source: North Bay Bohemian
